## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

16	用最通俗的语言过一遍本讲用到的概念，已有基础的读者可以跳过。
17	
18	- **DiT（Diffusion Transformer）**：一类用 Transformer 做去噪的扩散模型。视频生成的序列长度动辄数万 token（本项目的基准形状之一是 75827），注意力计算和通信都按序列长度增长。
19	- **序列并行（sequence parallelism）**：把一个长序列切成若干段，每张 GPU（每个 rank）持有其中一段。与按 batch 切分不同，序列并行让单卡放不下的长序列得以训练。
20	- **rank / world_size / 进程组**：分布式训练里每个参与进程是一个 rank，进程总数是 world_size（下文记作 ws）。`torch.distributed` 的进程组（process group）是它们互相通信的载体。本项目的算子是**集合通信**（collective）：所有 rank 一起调用同一个操作。
21	- **all-to-all**：每个 rank 都向其他所有 rank 发送一段数据、也从所有 rank 接收一段数据的通信模式。Ulysses 用它来完成「序列分片 ⇄ 头分片」的交换。
22	- **Ulysses 序列并行**：注意力前，一次 all-to-all 把「每卡一段序列、全部头」换成「全部序列、每卡一部分头」——注意力只依赖每个头内的序列，于是每卡可以独立算完注意力；再用第二次 all-to-all 换回来。两次通信把注意力计算包在中间。下一讲（u1-l2）会详细展开。

114	### 4.2 重排即步长
115	
116	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
117	
118	Ulysses 的 4D all-to-all 不是「把一整块连续内存原样发过去」：输入是 \((b, s_{\text{local}}, n_{\text{global}}, d)\)——本 rank 的序列段、全部的头；输出是 \((b, s_{\text{global}}, n_{\text{local}}, d)\)——全部序列、本 rank 的头。数据在内存里的排布必须随之重排。
119	
120	BASE 路径的做法分三步：先 `permute + contiguous` 把数据物理重排成「按目的 rank 分段、段内连续」的平坦缓冲，再 `all_to_all_single` 原样搬运，收完又 `permute + contiguous` 重排回目标布局。两次重排各要把整个张量**完整读写一遍**，且都跑在 SM 上。
121	
122	fast-ulysses 的洞察：`cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync` 这类「带步长拷贝」（pitched copy）本身就允许源和目的各配各的步长——搬运引擎在逐行搬运时**顺带完成了重排**。于是序列/头的排列被表达成每个拷贝操作的源/目的步长，两个 permute 内核整个消失。README 第二条特性「Relayout for free」说的就是这件事，并量化为「约是 `torch.distributed` 路径开销的一半」。
123	
124	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
125	
126	先建立带步长拷贝的直觉。一次 2D 拷贝的参数大致是：每行拷 `width` 字节，共 `rows` 行，源每前进一行跨 `spitch` 字节、目的每前进一行跨 `dpitch` 字节：
127	
128	\[ \text{src: } \text{addr} + r \cdot \text{spitch} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{dst: } \text{addr}' + r \cdot \text{dpitch}, \quad r = 0, 1, \dots, \text{rows}-1 \]
129	
130	选取不同的 \(\text{spitch}\) 与 \(\text{dpitch}\)，同样的字节流落进完全不同的布局——重排于是成为搬运的「副产品」，不再需要独立的内核。
131	
132	两条路径对比如下：
133	
134	```text
135	BASE:   x ──permute+contiguous(SM)──> 平坦缓冲 ──all_to_all_single──> 平坦接收
136	        ──reshape+permute+contiguous(SM)──> 输出
137	
138	OURS:   预先（纯主机）把交换算成一组 CopyOp{src_offset, dst_offset, pitch, width, rows}
139	        ──> 每个-op 变成一次 cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync（CE 执行，重排内嵌在步长里）
140	```
141	
142	关键差别：OURS 把「该搬哪些字节、按什么步长」的全部寻址**提前在主机上算完**（实现在 `src/a2a_plan.cc`，无 CUDA、无 torch，可在无 GPU 机器上测试），设备侧只剩纯搬运。

250	### 4.3 不均匀分片
251	
252	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
253	
254	序列并行要把全局序列长度 \(s\) 切成 ws 份。\(s\) 不一定能被 ws 整除——恰恰相反，真实工作负载几乎总不能：本项目基准的三个真实形状 \(s\) 都带着同一条 227 token 的文本尾巴。
255	
256	BASE 路径用的 `all_to_all_single`（平坦、等长段模式）要求每个 rank 的分片等长，所以必须把序列**补齐（padding）到 ws 的倍数**。补进来的假 token 不只是浪费通信字节：它们要跟着穿过**每一层的注意力和两次集合通信**，还要占激活内存。
257	
258	fast-ulysses 把这件事倒过来：调用方直接给出每个 rank 的 `seq_splits`（以及头轴的 `head_splits`），分片可以两两相差一个 token；**偶均分只是 `seq_splits = [s/P] * P` 的特例**，没有第二条代码路径。于是调用方可以直接扔掉 padding。
259	
260	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
261	
262	给定全局序列长 \(s\) 与 \(ws\) 个 rank，一种惯用的不均匀切法：
263	
264	\[ \text{base} = \left\lfloor s / ws \right\rfloor, \quad \text{rem} = s \bmod ws, \quad \text{seq\_splits}[i] = \text{base} + [i < \text{rem}] \]
265	
266	- 校验：\(\sum_i \text{seq\_splits}[i] = s\)，任意两份至多相差 1。
267	- BASE 的替代方案：\(s' = \lceil s / ws \rceil \cdot ws\)，补 \(s' - s \le ws - 1\) 个假 token，每 rank 拿 \(s'/ws\)。
268	- mode 0 的输入按 `seq_splits` 切序列轴、按 `head_splits` 合并头轴；输出形状由两组 splits 共同决定（细节在 u2-l3）。
269

309	   答：\(75827 = 4 \times 18906 + 3\)，所以 `seq_splits = [18907, 18907, 18907, 18906]`；BASE 补 \(4 - 3 = 1\) 个 token。
310	2. **问：为什么去掉 padding 对 BASE 反而要付 5–11%，而本路径几乎免费（1.00–1.03×）？**
311	   答：BASE 一旦分片不等长，就不能再用平坦 `all_to_all_single`，得换成带 split sizes 的调用、逐 peer reshape 再 `cat`，多出一轮重排；本路径的寻址本来就是按 per-rank splits 算的拷贝步长，不均分与均分走同一条代码路径。依据 [docs/benchmark.md:L188-L191](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L188-L191)、[docs/design.md:L41-L42](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L41-L42)。
312	3. **问：不均匀分片除了省通信字节，还省什么？**
313	   答：省掉假 token 穿过每层注意力与两次集合通信的计算与激活内存（[docs/benchmark.md:L330-L331](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L330-L331) 明确说这些是微基准看不见的端到端收益）。

410	## 6. 本讲小结
411	
412	- fast-ulysses 把 Ulysses 序列并行的 4D all-to-all 做成 `torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d`：长序列视频 DiT 中这两次集合通信正是关键路径。
413	- **零 SM 传输**：peer 拷贝是直写 peer 对称内存地址的带步长 `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync`，由拷贝引擎执行、不占 SM，可与 GEMM 完全重叠；端到端零 SM 还需用 `out=` 去掉占 SM 的 copy_out。
414	- **重排即步长**：序列/头排列被编码为拷贝的源/目的步长，BASE 的两个 permute 内核整个消失——这占 BASE 开销的 47–60%。
415	- **不均匀分片是一般路径**：per-rank `seq_splits`/`head_splits` 让调用方直接丢掉序列 padding（BASE 为此多付 5–11%，本路径 1.00–1.03×）。

417	- 适用边界同样明确：NVLink 单机、ws∈[1,8]、七个 dtype 且 \(d \times \text{elem\_size}\) 需 16 字节对齐、不可被 `torch.compile` trace、`out=`/async 不可微。
418	
419	## 7. 下一步学习建议
420	
421	- 下一讲 **u1-l2「Ulysses 序列并行原理」**：把本讲一笔带过的 mode 0 / mode 1 形状变换 \((b, s_{\text{local}}, n_{\text{global}}, d) \leftrightarrow (b, s_{\text{global}}, n_{\text{local}}, d)\) 讲透，并动手用 `split/cat` 实现等价变换。
422	- 想先把环境搭起来、亲手跑一次 `group.all_to_all_4d`，可先跳到 **u1-l3「安装、构建与第一次运行」**，对照 [README.md:L48-L74](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L48-L74) 的快速开始。
423	- 延伸阅读（本讲只节选了两段）：[docs/design.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md) 的其余部分论及未文档化的硬件假设与被否决的替代方案，第 9 单元会回头精读；[benchmark/bench_a2a.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py) 文件头的七种模式说明是理解性能文档的钥匙。

# fast-ulysses 是什么：用拷贝引擎搬运的 Ulysses all-to-all

## 1. 本讲目标

读完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 fast-ulysses 解决的核心问题：长序列视频 DiT（Diffusion Transformer）训练中，Ulysses 序列并行的两次 all-to-all 集合通信是关键路径，本项目把这一次 4D all-to-all 做成 torch 自定义算子。
2. 解释它的三条关键特性：**零 SM 传输**（peer 拷贝走拷贝引擎，不占计算单元）、**重排即步长**（序列/头的排列被编码成拷贝的源/目的步长，两个 permute 内核消失）、**不均匀分片是一般路径**（偶数均分只是特例）。
3. 对照 README 的限制清单（NVLink 单机、`world_size` 1–8、dtype 白名单与 16 字节对齐），判断自己的场景是否适用。
4. 按 docs/benchmark.md 的方法学读懂性能对比表，并亲手复算其中几个数字。

本讲不要求你写任何 CUDA 代码，也不需要多张 GPU——唯一需要跑代码的实践在单进程（CPU 或单卡）即可完成。

## 2. 前置知识

用最通俗的语言过一遍本讲用到的概念，已有基础的读者可以跳过。

- **DiT（Diffusion Transformer）**：一类用 Transformer 做去噪的扩散模型。视频生成的序列长度动辄数万 token（本项目的基准形状之一是 75827），注意力计算和通信都按序列长度增长。
- **序列并行（sequence parallelism）**：把一个长序列切成若干段，每张 GPU（每个 rank）持有其中一段。与按 batch 切分不同，序列并行让单卡放不下的长序列得以训练。
- **rank / world_size / 进程组**：分布式训练里每个参与进程是一个 rank，进程总数是 world_size（下文记作 ws）。`torch.distributed` 的进程组（process group）是它们互相通信的载体。本项目的算子是**集合通信**（collective）：所有 rank 一起调用同一个操作。
- **all-to-all**：每个 rank 都向其他所有 rank 发送一段数据、也从所有 rank 接收一段数据的通信模式。Ulysses 用它来完成「序列分片 ⇄ 头分片」的交换。
- **Ulysses 序列并行**：注意力前，一次 all-to-all 把「每卡一段序列、全部头」换成「全部序列、每卡一部分头」——注意力只依赖每个头内的序列，于是每卡可以独立算完注意力；再用第二次 all-to-all 换回来。两次通信把注意力计算包在中间。下一讲（u1-l2）会详细展开。
- **张量的形状（shape）与步长（stride）**：PyTorch 张量是一块一维内存加上「每个维度走一步跨多少元素」的描述，即步长。`x.permute(...)` 只改步长，不搬数据，几乎零成本（返回的是视图 view）；`x.contiguous()` 则要把数据按新布局**真正搬一遍**，分配新内存并启动一个拷贝内核。理解这一区别是理解本项目第二条特性的钥匙。
- **SM（Streaming Multiprocessor）**：GPU 上真正执行计算内核的单元，可以粗略理解为「GPU 的 CPU 核」。GEMM（矩阵乘）等计算内核会把 SM 吃满。
- **拷贝引擎（Copy Engine，CE，也叫 DMA 引擎）**：GPU 上独立于 SM 的专用搬运单元。`cudaMemcpyAsync` 一类的拷贝可以由 CE 执行，**完全不消耗 SM**——这就是本项目「计算和通信可以完全重叠」的硬件基础。
- **NVLink**：NVIDIA GPU 之间的高速互连总线，带宽远高于 PCIe。本项目的传输方式（跨步拷贝）在 NVLink 上高效，在 PCIe 上会严重退化，因此项目明确只支持单机 NVLink。
- **对称内存（symmetric memory）**：torch 提供的一种「每张卡都分配一块、且所有卡都能直接通过 NVLink 读写对方那块」的缓冲区。fast-ulysses 的传输就是拷贝引擎直接写进 peer 的对称内存地址。细节在第 4 单元展开，本讲只需知道这个名词。
- **bf16**：brain float 16，每个元素 2 字节，是本项目基准使用的 dtype。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 零 SM 传输

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

传统上，集合通信由 NCCL 这类库用**运行在 SM 上的内核**实现。问题在于：长序列 DiT 训练里，SM 同时也是 GEMM/注意力拼命抢占的资源——通信内核一启动，计算就得让路，两者无法完全重叠。

fast-ulysses 的做法：不写通信内核，直接用带步长的 `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync` 把数据拷进各 peer 的对称内存地址。这类拷贝由**拷贝引擎（CE）**执行，而 CE 是独立于 SM 的硬件单元，所以通信期间 SM 仍然 100% 留给计算内核——README 把这条列为第一条特性「No SMs」。

有两个必须分清的细节：

1. **零 SM 是「peer 拷贝」的性质**。同设备（device-to-device）的普通拷贝依然由 SM 执行、会和计算竞争。本库 copying 路径最后的 `copy_out`（窗口 → 调用者张量）就是这样一段同设备拷贝，因此「端到端零 SM」要靠 `out=`（从 `empty_output()` 拿缓冲）去掉 copy_out 才成立。
2. 这个论断不是口号，项目专门写了 `--mode zerosm` 的 A/B 基准去测量它（见 4.1.3）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把 BASE（`torch.distributed` 路径）与 fast-ulysses 各自的一次调用按「谁在执行」拆开：

```text
BASE（torch.distributed / sglang usp.py 路径）        fast-ulysses
──────────────────────────────────────────          ──────────────────────────────────────
① permute + contiguous   —— SM 上的拷贝内核          ① 屏障 barr_in（极短的自旋内核）
② all_to_all_single      —— 通信内核，也占 SM        ② peer 拷贝 ×(ws−1)  —— 拷贝引擎 CE，不占 SM
③ permute + contiguous   —— SM 上的拷贝内核             （本 rank 份额走调用者流，不跨链路）
                                                    ③ 屏障 barr_out
                                                    ④ copy_out —— 同设备拷贝，占 SM（out= 可去除）
```

注意对比的不对称性：BASE 的每一步都在 SM 上；fast-ulysses 只有屏障和 copy_out 碰 SM，而真正搬几百 MB 数据的 ② 完全在 CE 上。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

README 开头一段话就是问题陈述：Ulysses 序列并行需要两次 all-to-all，长序列视频 DiT 下这两次集合通信就是关键路径——见 [README.md:L11-L15](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L11-L15)，其中说明本库把它做成 `torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d`，跑在 NVLink 单机上。

第一条特性原文在 [README.md:L19-L22](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L19-L22)：peer 传输是直接射向 peer 对称内存地址的带步长 `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync`，因此跑在拷贝引擎上、计算内核保有全部 SM；括号里还给出了实测结论——peer 拷贝可与并发 GEMM 完全重叠，同设备拷贝不行，这正是 `out=` 更快的原因。

「零 SM 端到端」的精确表述在 [docs/benchmark.md:L142-L145](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L142-L145)：`copy_out` 是同设备拷贝，会和计算抢 SM，而 peer 拷贝不会；所以零拷贝路径（`out=`）才是真正端到端零 SM 的那条。

这个性质如何被测量：[benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L47-L53](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L47-L53) 是 `zerosm` 模式的说明——同样字节、同样次数的 `dst.copy_(src)`，一次写进 peer 的对称内存窗口、一次写本卡内存，各压一条按自己时长配平的 GEMM 链，同时读「GEMM 自身的慢化」和「两臂墙钟比」两个指标。设计文档 [docs/design.md:L25-L31](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L25-L31) 进一步说明为什么两臂要各配各的 GEMM 链：同样的字节到 peer 比到本机慢好几倍，一条链配不平两臂。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

1. **问：peer 拷贝能与 GEMM 完全重叠，同设备拷贝不能，根本原因是什么？**
   答：peer 拷贝由拷贝引擎（CE）执行，CE 是独立于 SM 的硬件单元；同设备拷贝走 SM 上的内核，与 GEMM 竞争同一批执行资源和内存系统。依据 [README.md:L19-L22](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L19-L22)、[docs/benchmark.md:L142-L145](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L142-L145)。
2. **问：既然传输零 SM，为什么说 copying 路径「不是端到端零 SM」？怎么补齐？**
   答：因为最后还有一步 `copy_out`（窗口 → 调用者张量）是同设备拷贝，占 SM。用 `empty_output()` 预先拿对称缓冲并经 `out=` 传入，peers 直写调用者缓冲，copy_out 消失，才是端到端零 SM。依据 [docs/benchmark.md:L142-L145](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L142-L145) 与 [README.md:L93](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L93)。
3. **问：`zerosm` 基准为什么不能只用「两臂墙钟比」一个指标下结论？**
   答：因为被拷贝「饿瘦」的 GEMM 也可能恰好读到 1.00×；必须把 GEMM 自身慢化和成对墙钟比放在一起读，两列各自都不能单独定案。依据 [benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L47-L53](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L47-L53)。

### 4.2 重排即步长

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

Ulysses 的 4D all-to-all 不是「把一整块连续内存原样发过去」：输入是 \((b, s_{\text{local}}, n_{\text{global}}, d)\)——本 rank 的序列段、全部的头；输出是 \((b, s_{\text{global}}, n_{\text{local}}, d)\)——全部序列、本 rank 的头。数据在内存里的排布必须随之重排。

BASE 路径的做法分三步：先 `permute + contiguous` 把数据物理重排成「按目的 rank 分段、段内连续」的平坦缓冲，再 `all_to_all_single` 原样搬运，收完又 `permute + contiguous` 重排回目标布局。两次重排各要把整个张量**完整读写一遍**，且都跑在 SM 上。

fast-ulysses 的洞察：`cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync` 这类「带步长拷贝」（pitched copy）本身就允许源和目的各配各的步长——搬运引擎在逐行搬运时**顺带完成了重排**。于是序列/头的排列被表达成每个拷贝操作的源/目的步长，两个 permute 内核整个消失。README 第二条特性「Relayout for free」说的就是这件事，并量化为「约是 `torch.distributed` 路径开销的一半」。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

先建立带步长拷贝的直觉。一次 2D 拷贝的参数大致是：每行拷 `width` 字节，共 `rows` 行，源每前进一行跨 `spitch` 字节、目的每前进一行跨 `dpitch` 字节：

\[ \text{src: } \text{addr} + r \cdot \text{spitch} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{dst: } \text{addr}' + r \cdot \text{dpitch}, \quad r = 0, 1, \dots, \text{rows}-1 \]

选取不同的 \(\text{spitch}\) 与 \(\text{dpitch}\)，同样的字节流落进完全不同的布局——重排于是成为搬运的「副产品」，不再需要独立的内核。

两条路径对比如下：

```text
BASE:   x ──permute+contiguous(SM)──> 平坦缓冲 ──all_to_all_single──> 平坦接收
        ──reshape+permute+contiguous(SM)──> 输出

OURS:   预先（纯主机）把交换算成一组 CopyOp{src_offset, dst_offset, pitch, width, rows}
        ──> 每个-op 变成一次 cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync（CE 执行，重排内嵌在步长里）
```

关键差别：OURS 把「该搬哪些字节、按什么步长」的全部寻址**提前在主机上算完**（实现在 `src/a2a_plan.cc`，无 CUDA、无 torch，可在无 GPU 机器上测试），设备侧只剩纯搬运。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

BASE 路径在项目里有真实可运行的实现——基准脚本里的 `baseline_padded`，见 [benchmark/bench_a2a.py:L140-L148](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/benchmark/bench_a2a.py#L140-L148)：

```python
def baseline_padded(x, pg, ws, recv) -> None:
    """usp.py mode 0: permute, flat all_to_all_single, permute. ..."""
    b, s_local, h_global, d = x.shape
    h_local = h_global // ws
    y = x.permute(2, 0, 1, 3).contiguous().flatten()        # 重排①：头提前，落成平坦发送缓冲
    dist.all_to_all_single(recv, y, group=pg)               # 搬运：平坦字节，不做重排
    z = recv.reshape(ws, h_local, b, s_local, d)
    z.permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4).contiguous().reshape(b, s_local * ws, h_local, d)  # 重排②
```

对照文档对这条路径的定义：[docs/benchmark.md:L64-L66](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L64-L66) —— `BASE` 是 `torch.distributed` 的「permute、`all_to_all_single`、permute」；`raw` 是单独的 `all_to_all_single`（同样字节、无重排、结果布局不对，因此只是传输下限而非可选项）。

本库一侧的论述在 [docs/design.md:L33-L35](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L33-L35)：序列/头的重排被表达为这些拷贝的源与目的步长，因此除了本来就必须发生的传输之外不花任何代价——这就是 BASE 的两个 permute 内核在本侧完全不存在的原因。README 特性原文见 [README.md:L23-L25](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L23-L25)。

#### 4.2.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：在单进程环境（CPU 或单卡）复现 BASE 路径的两次形状重排，实测 `permute + contiguous` 的真实开销，并亲手验证「permute 免费、contiguous 才搬数据」。

**操作步骤**（示例代码，保存为 `practice_relayout.py` 运行；只需 torch）：

```python
# 示例代码：单进程复现 BASE 的形状变换并计时
# 依据 benchmark/bench_a2a.py:140-148 的 baseline_padded
import time
import torch

ws = 8
b, s_local, h_global, d = 1, 4096, 40, 384   # 任务指定的形状；h_global=40 可被 ws=8 整除
h_local = h_global // ws
dev = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
x = torch.randn(b, s_local, h_global, d, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
nbytes = x.numel() * x.element_size()
print(f"字节数: {nbytes/1e6:.1f} MB  (设备: {dev})")

def relayout_in(x):                       # BASE 重排①（bench_a2a.py:145）
    return x.permute(2, 0, 1, 3).contiguous().flatten()

def relayout_out(recv):                   # BASE 重排②（bench_a2a.py:147-148）
```

### 4.3 不均匀分片

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

序列并行要把全局序列长度 \(s\) 切成 ws 份。\(s\) 不一定能被 ws 整除——恰恰相反，真实工作负载几乎总不能：本项目基准的三个真实形状 \(s\) 都带着同一条 227 token 的文本尾巴。

BASE 路径用的 `all_to_all_single`（平坦、等长段模式）要求每个 rank 的分片等长，所以必须把序列**补齐（padding）到 ws 的倍数**。补进来的假 token 不只是浪费通信字节：它们要跟着穿过**每一层的注意力和两次集合通信**，还要占激活内存。

fast-ulysses 把这件事倒过来：调用方直接给出每个 rank 的 `seq_splits`（以及头轴的 `head_splits`），分片可以两两相差一个 token；**偶均分只是 `seq_splits = [s/P] * P` 的特例**，没有第二条代码路径。于是调用方可以直接扔掉 padding。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

给定全局序列长 \(s\) 与 \(ws\) 个 rank，一种惯用的不均匀切法：

\[ \text{base} = \left\lfloor s / ws \right\rfloor, \quad \text{rem} = s \bmod ws, \quad \text{seq\_splits}[i] = \text{base} + [i < \text{rem}] \]

- 校验：\(\sum_i \text{seq\_splits}[i] = s\)，任意两份至多相差 1。
- BASE 的替代方案：\(s' = \lceil s / ws \rceil \cdot ws\)，补 \(s' - s \le ws - 1\) 个假 token，每 rank 拿 \(s'/ws\)。
- mode 0 的输入按 `seq_splits` 切序列轴、按 `head_splits` 合并头轴；输出形状由两组 splits 共同决定（细节在 u2-l3）。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

特性原文在 [README.md:L26-L27](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L26-L27)：per-rank 的 `seq_splits` / `head_splits` 正是让调用方得以丢弃序列 padding 的机制；偶均分是特例，不是单独的路径。

设计文档一句话给出了架构含义，见 [docs/design.md:L41-L42](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L41-L42)：不均匀分片是一般情况，偶均分就是 `seq_splits = [s/P] * P`；只有一条代码路径，所以只需要把一件事做对。

**实践目标**：为 docs/benchmark.md 的三个真实形状算出不均匀 splits 与 BASE 所需的 padding，发现它们共同的模式。

```python
def splits(total, ws):                     # 惯用切法：前 rem 个 rank 各多 1
    base, rem = divmod(total, ws)
    return [base + 1 if i < rem else base for i in range(ws)]

SHAPES = [("wan-720p", 75827, 40), ("wan-480p", 32987, 40), ("h3-t2va-5s", 38051, 56)]
for name, s, heads in SHAPES:
    ws = 8
    sp = splits(s, ws)
    pad = (-s) % ws                        # BASE 需要补齐的 token 数
    print(f"{name}: s={s}  seq_splits={sp}")
    print(f"  校验 sum={sum(sp)}=={s}  最大差={max(sp)-min(sp)}"
          f"  head_splits={splits(heads, ws)}  BASE 需 pad={pad} 个 token")
```

**需要观察的现象**：三个形状的 `seq_splits` 都是「3 个 rank 多 1、5 个 rank 少 1」；`pad` 全部等于 5；`head_splits` 全部均分。

**预期结果**：输出的 `sum` 与 `s` 相等、最大差为 1；pad=5 ≤ \(ws-1=7\)。三个形状 pad 相同并非巧合——它们的图像 token 数（75600/32760/37824）都能被 8 整除，而共同的 227 token 文本尾巴满足 \(227 \bmod 8 = 3\)，于是 \(\text{pad} = 8 - 3 = 5\)。这正是 [docs/benchmark.md:L32](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L32) 「s 含一条 227 token 的文本尾巴、因此不被组大小整除」的出处。

2. **问：复算 B300 wan-720p 行的 `relayout%`（perm_in 0.344、perm_out 0.366、BASE 1.184）。**
   答：\((0.344 + 0.366) / 1.184 = 59.97\% \approx 59.9\%\)，与表格一致（[docs/benchmark.md:L78](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/benchmark.md#L78)）。

4. **预期结果**：报告中应能回答三个问题——(a) 重排税在你的机器上占比多少（量级即可）；(b) 你的序列要不要 padding、要补几个 token；(c) 你的机器能否用这个库（若只有 PCIe 或跨 socket，结论应指向「不能用，构造函数会拒绝」，依据 4.4.3 的 PCIe 一节）。若在共享 GPU 或 CPU 上完成，注明数字不可与文档表直接比较（**待本地验证**：独占 GPU 上的数值）。

- fast-ulysses 把 Ulysses 序列并行的 4D all-to-all 做成 `torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d`：长序列视频 DiT 中这两次集合通信正是关键路径。
- **零 SM 传输**：peer 拷贝是直写 peer 对称内存地址的带步长 `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync`，由拷贝引擎执行、不占 SM，可与 GEMM 完全重叠；端到端零 SM 还需用 `out=` 去掉占 SM 的 copy_out。
- **重排即步长**：序列/头排列被编码为拷贝的源/目的步长，BASE 的两个 permute 内核整个消失——这占 BASE 开销的 47–60%。

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
